idiom_name: `object XxxMother` / top-level factory functions plus data-class defaults
implementation_notes: Kotlin data classes with default arguments (data class Customer(val name: String = "Ada", val tier: Tier = Tier.VIP)) absorb the common object-mother case directly: a valid baseline is one expression away and copy(tier = ...) covers variation. For multi-object graphs or named business states the idiomatic mother is a top-level object declaration - 'object CustomerMother { fun vip(name: String = "Ada") = Customer(...) }' - or plain top-level functions in src/test/kotlin; JUnit 5 or Kotest supply the test wiring, not the data. Prefer the object form for canonical named examples and data-class defaults for everything else.
pitfalls: Data-class copy() is shallow: overriding one field still shares the nested list or address instance with the original, so mutations leak between tests.
An object declaration is a process-wide singleton; if the mother caches instances or counts anything, parallel JUnit execution races.
Default arguments on production data classes make it impossible to tell intended values from fallbacks, in tests and production code alike.
Top-level factory functions in src/test are invisible to other modules' tests; move them to a testFixtures source set (or a test-support module) before copying them around.
